title: Matignon's tuple cipher: despatch to Henri III, May 1586 (BnF fr. 15572 ff. 234r-238v)

steps.what: Michael Brackx (issue #86): located the letter in BnF fr. 15572 (Gallica btv1b9061879d, canvases 240-247); cover 'Au Roy' endorsed May 1586 (Tomokiyo has March); canvas 243 duplicates 242; no leaf missing before f. 234r.
Brackx with Claude Code: all ten pages (220 lines) transcribed group by group from deskewed, flattened full-size canvases, the contemporary decipherer's glosses used to label groups; 136 labels.
Beam search over each label's allowed values under a French character 5-gram; key taken from the glosses and completed from the language.
Shuffled keys score about 35% of decoded letters in corpus words against 83.0% for the key.
Seven rounds of image checks; fixes were rows misaligned with the image, groups split over a line break entered twice, and mislabelled groups.
Brackx rebuilt the French model from the Essais I-III (Gutenberg 48529, 49168, 58801; 48530-31 were not Montaigne): coverage 80.8% of decoded letters (posted 83.0%), shuffled keys 28-30%.

Brackx: each page built into sentences in the decrypted spelling with every hole sized ([?] per unread group), an English translation with the same holes, the decryption laid against the transcription, and a 120-label legend tying labels to sign shapes.

Taken in here: read_share per page with v10_relabel.measure (in-word bracket expansions count as holes): 234r 0.987, 234v 0.622, 235r 0.962, 235v 0.954, 236r 0.723, 236v 0.431, 237r 0.92, 237v 0.929, 238r 0.803, 238v 0.756. All pages kept read in part, f. 236v decoded, not read, because 8-14% of groups per page are multi-valued labels chosen by the decoder, over the 3% look-alike limit.

Brackx (issue #95) recorded the contemporary gloss over each of the 107 multi-valued groups on 234r, 235r, 235v, 237r and 237v: 234r 20 agree, 1 contradicts, 3 unclear (unconfirmed 1.2%), so it meets the read bar; 235r 5/23 glossed, 235v 3/21, 237r 7/17, 237v 8/22. Four contradictions taken into the readings: 234r l. 7 qui (not que), 237r l. 1 de (not d), 237v ll. 3-4 monsieur (not sieur, twice). Re-measured: 234r 0.974 read, 237r 0.94, 237v 0.929.

Brackx (issue #99) recorded the glosses over the multi-valued groups on 234v, 236r, 236v, 238r, 238v (109 groups): 66 agree, 6 contradict, 9 unclear, 28 no gloss. All ten pages now checked: 114 of 2,135 groups unconfirmed (5.3%). Contradictions taken into the readings: 238r m'a dit auoir charge (0.803 -> 0.836), 236v cure remo[ns]trant. No class changes.

outcome.method_basis: The contemporary decipherer's interlinear glosses over most groups gave the key; Michael Brackx completed it from the language and decoded the unglossed groups with it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Word-weighted mean of the per-page read_share (v10_relabel.measure on texts/f*_reading.md: 1 - (holes + doubtful) / (words + holes)), all ten pages, f. 236v included.

gaps.item: multi-valued labels on the nine pages other than 234r (E2, M30, QUI, N18, DA and others)
gaps.detail: Every multi-valued group on all ten pages checked against the contemporary glosses (Brackx, issues #95 and #99; glosses_multivalued.tsv, 216 groups): 114 of 2,152 groups are not confirmed by a gloss (104 none or unclear, 10 contradicted and followed in the readings), and nothing else on the leaves settles them.

gaps.item: f. 236v, most of the page (read share 0.431)
gaps.detail: Show-through and faded ink; the mirrored-verso subtraction failed to register on ff. 236 and 238; much of the page rests on fragmentary glosses.

gaps.item: 234v l. 13 (groups between 'a quoy' and 'expense', name gloss 'Cadarran(?)') and ll. 21-24; 236r l. 15 and ll. 22-25; 238r ll. 20-22 ('la crois lartie'); 238v ll. 7-10 (a whole-word gloss read Bourg(?))
gaps.detail: Re-read letter by letter at full and upscaled resolution in the contributor's round 7; groups or glosses not resolved.

gaps.item: 41 rare 'open' labels (79 groups, 3.7%) whose sign shapes are not recorded
gaps.detail: Each occurs once or twice; legend.md gives where.

gaps.item: single-use values: 19 glossed sa on 236v (h elsewhere), QUAND, trouppes, X = paix, code 13 (faict?)
gaps.detail: One occurrence each; kept as one-off labels, not generalised.

texts.label: f. 234r
texts.summary: Opens mid-sentence: had the army stayed at Gabarret the writer would have gone that way, but with the Garonne trade cut off by 'the tyranny of those of Caumont' he advises going there to satisfy the captains, nobility and towns, who talk of a league among themselves.

reading_review.note: read_share 0.974 (v10_relabel.measure; the supplied [nt] in presente[nt] counts as a hole). The page is glossed group by group: Brackx recorded the contemporary gloss over all 24 multi-valued groups (glosses_multivalued.tsv, issue #95): 20 agree with the decoder, 1 contradicts it (l. 7, gloss qui over the group decoded que; the reading now follows the gloss) and 3 are unclear (l. 3 CN, l. 12 DAN and BQ). Unconfirmed choices 3 of 251 groups (1.2%), under the 3% look-alike limit.

texts.label: f. 234v
texts.summary: The poor people ruined by Huguenot contributions need help; a passage on expenses and commissions, and on the sieur de la Fontaine, is only partly read.

reading_review.note: Coherent sentences in the decrypted spelling, read as prose; read_share 0.622 (v10_relabel.measure, in-word bracket expansions counted as holes). Kept read in part whatever the share: 8-14% of groups on each page are multi-valued labels (E2, M30, QUI, N18, DA ...) whose value the decoder chose, over the 3% look-alike limit.

prior.where: Contemporary interlinear decipherment over most groups on the leaves themselves; Tomokiyo describes the cipher and the letter but gives neither key nor reading; no edition found.

human: Contributed: Michael Brackx (issue #86, 22-23 Oct 2026) transcribed, decoded and read all ten pages with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5); the project took it in on 24 Oct 2026, re-measured read shares and set the classes. No second person has checked the transcription against the images.
